newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-MUTED HOMECOMING FOR CHAMPION HINGIS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MUTED HOMECOMING FOR CHAMPION HINGIS.

text.p: Wimbledon champion Martina Hingis made a rare home appearance on Saturday to help Switzerland into a 2-0 lead over Argentina in their Fed Cup World Group one play-off.
Patty Schnyder also won her singles to leave Switzerland needing just one victory from Sunday's reverse singles and doubles to reach the top group next year.

While successful, it was hardly the homecoming the world number one might have expected. Only about half the 2,000 seats at the Saalsporthalle were filled for her first competitive match in Switzerland in almost a year.
The small crowd was treated to only a brief glimpse of the their 16-year-old heroine, as she romped home 6-1 6-2 against Maria Jose Gaidano in just 49 minutes.
Gaidano, ranked 130 places below Hingis, never threatened. She was completely helpless against the Swiss, who moved her around the court and fired winners at will.
Hingis was so relaxed that that she joked and laughed during changeovers with her mother and coach Melanie Molitor, who joined her on the court as captain of the Swiss team.

"I didn't have any problems with the change from Wimbledon even though it's another speed on carpet," said Hingis. "My serves were good and I could go up to the net often because she didn't return very well."
If the low attendance was a disappointment, Hingis refused to let it show. "To me it's not important if the stands are full. My job is to play top tennis," she said.
While Hingis eased into the competition, Schnyder had the job of facing Argentina's top ranked player, number 37 Florencia Labat.
Schnyder, who has steadily worked her way up the world rankings to number 32 but is destined to toil in Hingis' shadow, triumphed 3-6 7-5 10-8 in two hours 26 minutes.
